request.statement:
/**
Classify every Unicode scalar value in a source file as executable, comment, or quoted text.

Submit one complete Rust program containing `fn main()`. Use only the Rust standard library.

Input consists of an ASCII decimal integer `N`, one LF byte, then exactly `N` bytes of valid UTF-8 source text. `0 <= N <= 2_000_000`. The source may contain any Unicode scalar values, including newlines, and may end inside any construct.

Output one token containing exactly one letter per Unicode scalar value, in source order: `E` for executable text, `C` for comments, and `Q` for quoted text. For an empty source, output an empty line.

Recognition is left-to-right. All syntax characters below are ASCII. In executable text, apply these rules in precedence order:

1. `#` starts a line comment. It and everything before the next LF are `C`; that LF is not part of the comment.
2. `/*` starts a nested block comment. Everything through its matching `*/` is `C`; nested `/*` increases the depth. No other syntax is recognized inside it.
3. `'''` and `"""` start triple-quoted literals; otherwise `'` and `"` start ordinary quoted literals. Delimiters are `Q`.
4. A sigil starts with `~`, one ASCII letter, and either `(`, `[`, `{`, `<`, `/`, `|`, or a triple quote. Its prefix and opening delimiter are `Q`. Paired delimiters close with `)`, `]`, `}`, `>` and nest using their own opener. `/` and `|` close at their next unescaped occurrence.
5. `?` begins an entirely executable character form. It consumes the next scalar value; if that value is `\`, it also consumes one further scalar value. Missing values at EOF are ignored.

A triple-quoted literal or sigil is a heredoc exactly when its opening delimiter is immediately followed by zero or more spaces or tabs and then LF. Otherwise it is an ordinary triple-quoted construct. An ordinary triple construct closes at the next matching triple quote. A heredoc closes only at a matching triple quote whose first quote is the first non-space-or-tab scalar on its physical line. The start of the source and every position after LF begin a physical line. Quotes elsewhere in a heredoc are content. Leading spaces and tabs before its closing delimiter remain `Q`.

Inside every quoted construct, `\` and the following scalar value are `Q` and cannot open, close, or interpolate. If no following scalar exists, only `\` is consumed.

Double-quoted literals interpolate; single-quoted literals do not. A sigil interpolates exactly when its letter is lowercase ASCII. In an interpolating construct, unescaped `#{` is `E` and begins embedded executable text. Braces in that text nest; the matching `}` is `E` and resumes the quoted construct. All executable rules apply inside interpolation, so nested constructs may hide braces. Physical-line heredoc closing eligibility is determined from the original source, including text inside interpolations.

Any construct still open at EOF extends to EOF. Characters not consumed by a rule are `E`.
*/
